correctness.rationale: Exact normalized first and second moments yield the variance polynomial. The derivative critical points are in (1/2,2^(-1/m)). Its turning function has numerator H_m. Seven positive exact Bernstein certificates prove H_m>0 for m=2..6. For m>=7 three signs and Descartes give exactly two extrema of h_m and hence a nonempty squared-length interval with two variance maxima. The strictly positive eight-tip tree has an independently verified polynomial and exactly three derivative zeros by rational sign brackets and a three-sign-change upper bound. The finite checks support but do not replace the infinite m argument.

value.rationale: Rooted future-PD variance measures biodiversity risk beyond its mean, and changing a common survival probability is a natural scenario parameter. The theorem reveals a genuine two-scale variance-peak competition (singleton lineage versus all-or-nothing clade retention), with an exact all-family cutoff and a strictly positive-edge realization. It is a meaningful qualitative boundary not an isolated arbitrary numerical table. It makes no empirical or global-minimum claim.
